page: Microsoft Azure E96-24ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EADSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The server is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 28.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is bundled with 3686 GB of SSD capacity, and the instance does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance scoring 2905.99, placing it in the top 25% of tested hardware. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng is average at 32377.42. Memory performance is a key strength, highlighted by a strong Passmark memory score of 2854.45, though large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidths remain average at 59.95 GB/sec and 33.92 GB/sec respectively. For language model workloads, the server achieves a strong text generation speed of 291.13 tokens/sec on small 135M models, but exhibits poor prompt processing performance of 4.98 tokens/sec on large 70B models.

The E96-24ads_v5 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require massive memory footprints relative to compute capacity, allowing organizations to run large in-memory databases or data-intensive applications without paying for unnecessary extra vCPUs. The combination of 672.0 GB of RAM and 3686 GB of local SSD storage makes this server highly suitable for memory-heavy databases, large-scale data caching, enterprise resource planning systems, and memory-bound ETL pipelines.
